notes: This is an alpine track on active volcanoes. The weather changes fast. Snow is possible in any month.
Read the volcanic alert level before you go. If there is an eruption, move away from the vents and out of the valleys.
Do not drink from the lakes and streams near the craters. Fill your bottles at the huts.
In the cold months you need alpine skills and equipment, or a guide.

waihohonu.name: Waihohonu Hut and Campsite
waihohonu.note: DOC hut and campsite. You must book before you go. Facilities: cooking, heating, mattresses, non-flush toilets. Boil the water before you drink it.

start.name: Whakapapa Village
start.note: Start and end of the circuit. The visitor centre has the weather and the volcanic alert level.

pois.name: Emerald Lakes
pois.text: Three small crater lakes. Minerals from the hot ground give the green colour. The water is acid: do not touch it.

pois.name: Blue Lake
pois.text: A cold acid lake in an old crater. The lake is tapu: do not eat or drink at its shore.

pois.name: Soda Springs
pois.text: Cold springs with yellow buttercups in summer, a short side track from the head of the Mangatepopo valley.

pois.name: Taranaki Falls
pois.text: Waterfall of 20 m over the edge of an old lava flow, about 1 hour from Whakapapa Village.

pois.name: Tama Lakes
pois.text: Two crater lakes between Ngauruhoe and Ruapehu. The side track to the lower lake lookout takes about 20 minutes there and back from the junction.

pois.name: Ohinepango Springs
pois.text: Cold springs that come out below an old lava flow, about 1 hour there and back from Waihohonu Hut.

pois.name: Old Waihohonu Hut
pois.text: Built in 1904 for coach travellers. It is the oldest mountain hut in New Zealand.

pois.name: Red Crater
pois.text: The highest point of the circuit, 1886 m. Heat changed the iron in the rock to red. The loose rock on the descent to the Emerald Lakes is slippery.
